messages:
erin: Quick sync — Q4 roadmap decision needed for Dedicated autoscale lanes + burst behavior. Customers asking for predictable SLAs but want cheaper baseline. Thoughts on proposal below?

Proposal:
- Two lane types: steady (reserved, strict SLA) + elastic (cheaper, preemptible with burst spots)
- Autoscale policy: steady = guaranteed concurrency, elastic = scale to N when steady exhausted, best-effort fallback
- Launch criteria: perf tests, billing model, safety rails for noisy tenants, evictions <= 0.5% p95 during peak

sandeep: +1 on two lanes. question: how strict is "guaranteed concurrency"? is that per-account or per-reservation?

erin: per-reservation for Dedicated. per-account mapping configurable. goal is contractual guarantees to enterprise customers.

jules: Implementation notes from runtime POV: we can implement elastic as preemptible worker pool with signal for KV cache flush. eviction path will add ~60–120ms tail latency for affected requests.

maya: From evals: model quality regression when we switch to elastic quantized variants under load. need gating test set and automatic rollback on score delta > 1.5% on key prompts.

tony: Customers care about carve-outs for compliance. If elastic can land on shared infra, some customers will require isolation -> we'll need an isolation opt-in flag for Dedicated customers.

erin: Agreed. propose: dedicated.reserved = locked GPUs; dedicated.elastic = isolated per-tenant VMs, still preemptible but no co-tenant model sharing for regulated customers. Thoughts?

sandeep: That's more complex infra-wise but cleaner from product. Also need escape hatch for noisy tenants: soft-preempt (notify client, 30s drain) vs hard-evict. Which do we pick for launch?

jules: Soft-preempt first. We can implement drain hooks in runtime and fall back to hard-evict if drain fails after TTL. Metrics to track: drain success rate, time-to-evict, % requests retried.

erin: Launch criteria draft (please comment):
- Performance: p95 latency within 1.2x steady lane under 95th percentile loads
- Reliability: eviction rate <= 0.5% per week for elastic lane
- Cost: elastic lane reduces committed cost by >=15% for sample workloads
- Safety: regression alerting integrated with rollouts (auto rollback on eval delta)
- Compliance: isolation flag works and tested for at least 2 regulated customers

maya: Add: end-to-end test harness that runs busywork for 6h with model mix + 10% synthetic spikes. verify token correctness and throughput.

tony: Also require pricing docs and a clear FAQ: what happens to long-running streams during an eviction? (answer: drain then reconnect flow).

erin: Good call. I'll add that to launch checklist.

jules: One more ops ask: telemetry we need to ship day 1: per-request lane tag, eviction reason, preemptible-worker-id, and cache-warmth flag. sample metric names: `dedicated.lane.evictions`, `dedicated.lane.drain_success`, `dedicated.lane.tail_latency`.

sandeep: For rollout plan: 1) internal dogfood on small fleet, 2) invite-only customers (2–3), 3) general availability. Each stage gated by the criteria above.

erin: Proposed owners: product = erin, runtime infra = jules, ML evals = maya, customer pilots = tony, PMM/docs = sasha (cc @sasha).

deploy-bot: Reminder: Feature branch `feat/dedicated-elastic-lanes` created at commit abc123. CI: pending.

erin: Next steps: jules + sandeep to draft a high-level spec this week, maya to prototype gating tests, tony to line up pilot customers. I'll consolidate into a launch ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sandeep: ack. I'll start a sketch of autoscale policy config. snippet idea:```json
{"policy": "elastic", "min_replicas": 0, "burst_limit": 200, "preemptible_ttl": 30}
```

jules: tagging for follow-up: @maya please list the eval prompts for regression checks; @tony please send pilot customer contacts.

maya: will do, adding prompts to the eval repo and linking in the ticket.

tony: sending customer list this afternoon.

erin: closing the thread for now — will open a formal GH spec and roadmap ticket. will ping when ready. :calendar:
